classification.difficultyReason: Identify the side opposite the smallest angle, use the cosine rule, then connect its exact cosine to positive sine and the triangle area rule while retaining radicals.

content.prompt: In a triangle with sides $9\text{ cm}$, $7\text{ cm}$ and $4\text{ cm}$, find $\cos\alpha$, where $\alpha$ is the smallest angle, and hence show that the exact area is $6\sqrt5\text{ cm}^2$.

answer.short:
$\cos\alpha=\frac{19}{21}$; exact area $=6\sqrt5\text{ cm}^2$.

Use the cosine rule, find positive $\sin\alpha$, then apply the area rule.
answer.worked:
The smallest angle is opposite the $4\text{ cm}$ side. By the cosine rule,
$\begin{align*}\cos\alpha&=\frac{9^2+7^2-4^2}{2(9)(7)}\\\cos\alpha&=\frac{114}{126}\\\cos\alpha&=\frac{19}{21}.\end{align*}$
Since $\alpha$ is an interior angle, $\sin\alpha>0$.
$\begin{align*}\sin\alpha&=\sqrt{1-\left(\frac{19}{21}\right)^2}\\\sin\alpha&=\sqrt{\frac{80}{441}}\\\sin\alpha&=\frac{4\sqrt5}{21}\\\operatorname{Area}&=\tfrac12(9)(7)\frac{4\sqrt5}{21}\\\operatorname{Area}&=6\sqrt5\text{ cm}^2.\end{align*}$
